messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Kannada, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Requirements (ONE Markdown table): - Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] - In [Target Requirement], make comparative direction unambiguous and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Output: ONLY the table; no extra prose.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement (Kannada morphosyntax) | |-------------|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------| | **Tant'** | Intensifier indicating a high degree of bitterness. | Use degree adverb **ತುಂಬ** *tumba* (intensifier) modifying the adjective; back‑translation check: “so”. | | **è** (1) | Copular verb linking implicit subject “it” to predicate “bitter”. | Present‑tense copula **ಇದೆ** *ide*; back‑translation check: “is”. | | **amara** | Predicate adjective denoting the property “bitter”. | Adjective **ಕಹಿ** *kahi* (bitter) agreeing with the subject (no inflection needed); back‑translation check: “bitter”. | | **che** | Comparative subordinator introducing the clause “death is a little more”. | Comparative complementizer **ಎಂದು** *endu* (that) introducing a comparative clause; back‑translation check: “that”. | | **poco** | Adverb quantifying the degree of increase as “little”. | Degree adverb **ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ** *svalpa* placed before the comparative adverb; back‑translation check: “little”. | | **è** (2) | Copular verb linking “death” to the comparative predicate. | Present‑tense copula **ಇದೆ** *ide*; back‑translation check: “is”. | | **più** | Comparative adverb meaning “more” (with a slight excess). | Comparative adverb **ಹೆಚ್ಚು** *hecchu* combined with the comparative particle **ಕ್ಕಿಂತ** *kkintha* to mark “more than”; back‑translation check: “more”. | | **morte** | Noun denoting “death”, the benchmark of bitterness. | Noun **ಮರಣ** *marana* in nominative (subject) case; back‑translation check: “death”. | | **ma** | Coordinating conjunction signalling contrast. | Conjunction **ಆದರೆ** *adare* (but); back‑translation check: “but”. | | **per** | Preposition marking purpose (“in order to”). | Purpose marker **ಗಾಗಿ** *gaagi* attached to the infinitive; back‑translation check: “for”. | | **trattar** | Infinitive verb “to treat / discuss”. | Infinitive **ಚರ್ಚಿಸಲು** *charchisalu* (to discuss) with the infinitive suffix **‑ಲು**; back‑translation check: “to treat”. | | **del** | Partitive preposition “of the”. | Genitive construction **ದ** *da* attached to the noun (e.g., **ಮಂಗಳದ** *mangalada*); back‑translation check: “of the”. | | **ben** | Abstract noun “good”. | Noun **ಮಂಗಳ** *mangala* in genitive case when combined with **ದ**; back‑translation check: “good”. | | **ch'i'** | Relative clause introducer “that I”. | Relative pronoun **ಅದು** *adu* + first‑person pronoun **ನಾನು** *naanu* forming **ಅದು ನಾನು**; back‑translation check: “that I”. | | **vi** | Locative adverb “there”. | Locative adverb **ಅಲ್ಲಿ** *alli*; back‑translation check: “there”. | | **trovai** | Simple past verb “found”. | Past‑tense verb **ಹುಡುಕಿದೆ** *hudukide* (found) with past marker **‑ಇತ್ತು**; back‑translation check: “found”. | | **dirò** | Future verb “I will tell”. | Future‑tense verb **ಮಾತು ಹೇಳುವೆನು** *maatu heluvenu* (will say) with future marker **‑ುವೆನು**; back‑translation check: “will tell”. | | **de** | Preposition “of”. | Genitive marker **ನಿಂದ** *ninda* (from/of) attached to the noun phrase; back‑translation check: “of”. | | **l'altre** | Determiner + adjective “the other”. | Demonstrative‑adjective **ಇತರ** *ithara* with definite sense (contextualized as “the other”); back‑translation check: “the other”. | | **cose** | Plural noun “things”. | Noun **ವಸ್ತುಗಳು** *vastugalu* in plural nominative; back‑translation check: “things”. | | **ch'i'** (2) | Relative clause introducer “that I”. | Same as above: **ಅದು ನಾನು** *adu naanu*; back‑translation check: “that I”. | | **v'ho** | Perfect auxiliary with locative clitic “there”. | Perfect auxiliary **ಇದಿದೆ** *ide* plus locative clitic **ಅಲ್ಲಿ** *alli* → **ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಇತ್ತು** *alli ittu* (have there); back‑translation check: “have … there”. | | **scorte** | Past participle “seen” agreeing with plural “things”. | Past participle **ಕಾಣಿದ್ದ** *kāṇidda* agreeing in number with **ವಸ್ತುಗಳು**; back‑translation check: “seen”. |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Create placeable Kannada components for Step 4. Output ONLY bullet list; ONE LINE per bullet. - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Where <ID> is the leading integer at the start of the source line. Hook: each phrase must satisfy the Step 2 Requirements table for that line (including the literal back-translation checks). Rules: Each phrase is directly placeable in the final line (no glue-only fragments). Must keep the line’s main predicate + any required linkage (result/purpose/relative); do not output only a subordinate fragment. Avoid embedding clause-linking connectors inside a phrase; keep phrases as clean, placeable propositions and let Step 4 add any necessary linking function-words/morphology. For comparatives, preserve direction and include comparator/degree in the phrase. No punctuation characters inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 7: ಅದು ತುಂಬ ಕಹಿ ಆಗಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಮರಣವು ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಕಹಿ / ಅದು ತುಂಬ ಕಹಿ ಆಗಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಮರಣಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಕಹಿ / ಅದು ತುಂಬ ಕಹಿ ಆಗಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಮರಣವು ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಕಹಿ
- Line 8: ಆದರೆ ಮಂಗಳದ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಚರ್ಚಿಸಲು ನಾನು ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿದ / ಆದರೆ ಮಂಗಳವನ್ನು ಚರ್ಚಿಸಲು ನಾನು ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿದ / ಆದರೆ ಮಂಗಳದ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಚರ್ಚಿಸಲು ನಾನು ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಡು
- Line 9: ಅಲ್ಲಿ ನಾನು ಕಂಡಿರುವ ಇತರ ವಸ್ತುಗಳ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ನಾನು ಹೇಳುವೆನು / ನಾನು ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಡಿರುವ ಇತರ ವಸ್ತುಗಳ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಹೇಳುವೆನು / ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಡಿರುವ ಇತರ ವಸ್ತುಗಳ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ನಾನು ಹೇಳುವೆನು

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Assemble Step3 components into Kannada lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 Final Form as contiguous substrings; reorder within-line as needed. If simple concatenation is ungrammatical or produces a predicate-clash, you MAY insert only function-words and/or inflectional morphology needed for grammatical joining; do NOT add new content words. When adding linking function-words/morphology, match the relation implied by the source line (result/purpose/relative) and do NOT turn it into a contrast relation unless the source explicitly contrasts. Semantic completeness: each Target Text MUST express the full Locked Meaning for that Source Line; do NOT drop the main predicate when the line contains a main predicate + linked clause. Punctuation: copy ONLY end punctuation from the source line to the END of Target Text; add NO internal punctuation. For each source line output ONLY this block (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary phrase from Step 3: re-insert it (no new content words).

**Source Line:** 7 Tant' è amara che poco è più morte;
**Line Inventory:** - ಅದು ತುಂಬ ಕಹಿ ಆಗಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಮರಣವು ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಕಹಿ
**Assembly Notes:** - Added copular verb *ಇದೆ* after the comparative predicate to satisfy the required “is” in Kannada.
**Target Text:** ಅದು ತುಂಬ ಕಹಿ ಆಗಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಮರಣವು ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಕಹಿ ಇದೆ.
---
**Source Line:** 8 ma per trattar del ben ch'i' vi trovai,
**Line Inventory:** - ಆದರೆ ಮಂಗಳದ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಚರ್ಚಿಸಲು ನಾನು ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿದ
**Assembly Notes:** - No additional function‑words needed; the phrase already contains the contrast conjunction *ಆದರೆ* and the purpose infinitive *ಚರ್ಚಿಸಲು*.
**Target Text:** ಆದರೆ ಮಂಗಳದ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಚರ್ಚಿಸಲು ನಾನು ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿದ,
---
**Source Line:** 9 dirò de l'altre cose ch'i' v'ho scorte.
**Line Inventory:** - ನಾನು ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಡಿರುವ ಇತರ ವಸ್ತುಗಳ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಹೇಳುವೆನು
**Assembly Notes:** - No extra morphology required; the future verb *ಹೇಳುವೆನು* and perfect participle *ಕಂಡಿರುವ* convey the locked meaning.
**Target Text:** ನಾನು ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಡಿರುವ ಇತರ ವಸ್ತುಗಳ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಹೇಳುವೆನು.

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check Verify each Step4 line vs Reference Translation + Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within the line; re-insert only Step4 Missing; fix function-word/morphology anywhere; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation rule: do NOT introduce new internal punctuation; only keep the end punctuation transferred from the source line. Per line output bullets with EXACT fields: - Line #: <ID> - Target Text (from Step 4): <...> - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): <...> - Reference Translation (line-aligned): <...> - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> - If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text: <...> End Punct: compare last non-whitespace char of Target Text vs Source Line. Line # rule: <ID> is the leading integer at the start of that Source Line. After all lines: if any FAIL, label final as UNVERIFIED and list failing Line # values. Output final Kannada text in ONE code block, line by line.

- Line #: 7 - Target Text (from Step 4): ಅದು ತುಂಬ ಕಹಿ ಆಗಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಮರಣವು ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಕಹಿ ಇದೆ. - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): It is very bitter, that death is a little more bitter. - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): So bitter is it that death is little more. - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **FAIL**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **OK**, Hallucination **OK** - Corrected Target Text: ಅದು ತುಂಬ ಕಹಿ ಆಗಿದೆ ಎಂದು ಮರಣವು ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಕಹಿ ಇದೆ;
- Line #: 8 - Target Text (from Step 4): ಆದರೆ ಮಂಗಳದ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಚರ್ಚಿಸಲು ನಾನು ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿದ, - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): But to discuss the good, I found there, - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): But in order to treat of the good that there I found, - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 9 - Target Text (from Step 4): ನಾನು ಅಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಡಿರುವ ಇತರ ವಸ್ತುಗಳ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಹೇಳುವೆನು. - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): I will tell about the other things that I have seen there. - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): I will tell of the other things that I have seen there. - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
**UNVERIFIED** – Failing Line(s): 7
